**Session note:** this workspace isn't a git repo and has no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or check open items. I didn't change any files, so there's no NOTES entry to add.

**Crew plan (single shot)**
- **Brief:** a still environment plate with no people, for compositing. Banana Pro (Higgsfield default), Mode 3B, 16:9. My assumption is that people get composited in later, seated at the near side of the table or standing at the window.
- **Director:** this is the room where the mine's decisions get made. You see the pit through the glass, so it frames every meeting. The room should feel working, not glossy.
- **Production design:** a renovated older office building with a modest 2026 refit. There's a long wood-laminate table and grey mesh chairs, and core-sample trays with green copper staining on a credenza. Hard hats and hi-vis vests hang on a stand. A wall display is switched off. The one personal touch is a set of tea glasses on saucers. The window is a corner ribbon window looking onto a terraced open pit, with low cloud and late-November snow on the ridges. All text is unreadable.
- **DP:** eye-level camera at about 125 cm, 28 mm-equivalent spherical lens, deep focus. The key light is the overcast window light from camera-right. The window view and the interior are both held with detail. Following studio rule §8, the plate is kept neutral: no grain, no grade, no vignette, no flare. I swapped the skill's usual grain, grade and flare close for a clean one.
- **Clean zone:** the near half of the table and the floor at camera-left are left clear for the actors.

## FINAL

**Mode 3B: environment plate (no people), Banana Pro, 16:9**

**Settings:** Higgsfield → Banana Pro (Nano Banana Pro) · Aspect ratio **16:9** · Resolution **4K** (2K for test runs) · No references · 2–4 variations · Don't write the aspect ratio into the prompt.

```
A clean, neutral photographic environment plate of an empty meeting room in the office of a copper mining company in the southern Armenian highlands, present day, late November, taken from eye level at the near end of a long conference table, the camera at seated-to-standing height looking down the length of the room toward a wide corner window, the table running from the lower-left foreground diagonally into the middle of the frame, the near half of the table and the open floor in the left foreground left clear and uncluttered as space for people to be added later, the composition calm, level and documentary, verticals kept straight.

The room is a renovated older administrative building with a modest recent refit: a long wood-grain laminate conference table with slightly worn edges, eight grey mesh office chairs tucked in at slightly uneven angles, light grey painted walls, grey commercial carpet tiles, a white panelled radiator under the window, a ceiling of square acoustic tiles with the overhead lights switched off. On the right wall a large wall-mounted display is switched off, its black glass showing a faint reflection of the window. Along the left wall a low credenza holds two long shallow wooden trays of drill-core samples, grey rock cylinders streaked with green copper staining and rusty ochre bands, each tray marked with small handwritten labels too faint to read at this distance. Beside it is a coat stand with two white hard hats and a folded orange high-visibility vest, a pair of dusty work boots standing on a sheet of cardboard on the floor beneath it. On the table are a rolled-up geological section drawing held flat at one end by a stapler, a black conference speakerphone in the centre, a glass carafe of water, and at the far end a small tray of clear tulip-shaped tea glasses on saucers with a half-full sugar bowl, left behind from the last meeting. A framed technical map of the pit's terraced benches hangs on the left wall, its lines and labels unreadable at this distance.

The far wall and the right-hand corner are one wide ribbon window in plain aluminium frames, and through it the open-pit copper mine fills the view: an enormous stepped crater cut into the mountainside, its terraced benches in rust ochre, ash grey and dull green-grey oxidised bands, a switchback haul road climbing the benches, three small yellow haul trucks parked far down on one bench, a fine pale dust film on the outside sill and lower glass. Beyond the pit, bare brown highland ridges rise into a low, even, pale grey overcast, the upper slopes dusted with early snow, the cloud base touching the highest ridge, the far distance softened by real atmospheric haze. The exterior view is held with full detail in the window, never burnt out, at a believable brightness above the room.

Soft overcast daylight from the window is the only key light, falling from camera-right and from the far end of the room, so the side of every object facing camera-right is lit and the side facing camera-left falls into gentle open shade. The brightest values are the overcast sky and the white hard hats; the darkest are under the table and inside the black display, with detail kept in the shadows and nothing crushed to black. Soft contact shadows sit under the chair bases, the carafe, the core trays and the boots, and a soft window-shaped glow lies on the near tabletop. Even, balanced exposure across the whole frame, with a neutral daylight white balance and true colours.

Shot as a clean modern digital still on a 28mm-equivalent rectilinear spherical lens at a moderate aperture, everything sharp from the foreground table edge to the distant ridges, low noise, natural micro-contrast, neutral and ungraded so that the final look can be added after compositing. Real photographic frame of a real room, real laminate, real mesh fabric, real rock cores, real glass and real mountain air: no people, no grain, no colour grade, no vignette, no lens flare, no bloom, no CGI, no rendered look, no plastic surfaces, no AI smoothness, no readable text or logos.
```

**QA:**
- **Framing:** 16:9, level verticals, clean zone at the near side and camera-left.
- **Light:** the key comes from camera-right/window. Brightest and darkest values are named, and contact shadows are kept.
- **Neutral plate:** no grain, grade, vignette or flare.
- **Text:** all unreadable. No real company, brand or logo.
- **Rights:** I wrote a generic southern-highlands pit rather than a named real mine. If it needs to read as a specific site, that's your call on location use. If so, add a real photo of that site as a place reference and say which parts of it the prompt should take.
- **If the window clips:** regenerate and add "the exterior one stop brighter than the room, never white".
